newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia hopes Burma will join ASEAN this year.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia hopes Burma will join ASEAN this year.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Wednesday that Jakarta hoped Burma, Cambodia and Laos would become full members of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) this year.
Speaking to reporters after meeting President Suharto, he said ASEAN continued to follow a policy of constructive engagement towards Burma.
"Our hope is that we will reach a consensus that those three nations can become full members this year," Alatas said.

ASEAN has come under Western pressure to at least delay Burma's entry into the regional grouping over Rangoon's human rights record and suppression of the nation's democracy movement. Washington, citing "severe repression" in Burma, imposed economic sanctions on the country earlier this month.
"Constructive engagement is more effective, compared with the approach of our dialogue partners, which will not be productive," Alatas said.
A senior Cambodian official said on Tuesday that ASEAN would admit Burma, Cambodia, and Laos at the end of this year, not in July as previously expected.
The three countries had hoped to join ASEAN at the seven-member group's ministerial meeting on July 24-25.
Alatas said ASEAN foreign ministers would meet in Kuala Lumpur on Saturday to decide when to admit the three.

He said he hoped the differences between ASEAN and its dialogue partners, including the United States, Japan and the European Union, would not disturb their relations when Burma, Cambodia and Laos were admitted.
"We are certainly watching the development in Myanmar (Burma) and other countries. The country's domestic problem and development are not criteria to become an ASEAN member," he said.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
